title: Best Electric Scooters UK (Private Land Only)
short: Electric scooters compared on range, ride comfort and build after two weeks of testing each. In the UK, privately owned e-scooters can only legally be ridden on private land.
intro: Important: in the UK it is illegal to ride a privately owned e-scooter on roads, pavements or in public spaces such as parks, because they can't currently be insured. They can only be ridden legally on private land with the landowner's permission, or you can use a rental scooter that's part of an official ride-share scheme. This guide compares scooters tested by TechRadar, who used each for at least two weeks for errands, commuting and exploring, testing acceleration, brakes, hill climbing, battery life and folding. TechRadar's page was last updated in December 2024.

products.name: Air Pro (2nd generation)
products.best_for: Experienced riders who want range and a solid build for private-land use
products.key_spec: 15.5mph top speed, up to 31 miles range at slower speeds, 16.5kg, IP65, folds
products.summary: TechRadar's top pick, with solid build quality and an impressive maximum range of about 50km (31 miles) if you ride at a more sedate pace. In testing the suspension ironed out small bumps and acceleration felt smooth, and the air-filled tyres use a puncture-resistant fluid, though it's heavy to carry and pushing the speed drains the battery quickly.
pros: Folds easily with a sturdy catch
cons: Battery drains quickly at high speeds

products.name: Air
products.best_for: First-time riders who want something dependable at a lower price
products.key_spec: 15.5mph top speed, 18 miles range, 16.5kg, IP65, lights and reflectors fitted
products.summary: TechRadar called this the best value e-scooter they've reviewed, recommended for a first ride or something dependable and long-lasting. It's sturdy, fitted with lights and reflectors, and was safe and comfortable to ride in testing, though it's still quite heavy (though lighter than the Pro) and the battery drains fast at top speed.
cons: Battery drains fast at top speed

products.name: KQi3 Pro
products.best_for: Riders on rough ground who prioritise comfort and features over low weight
products.key_spec: 20mph top speed, 31 miles range, 9.5in fat tyres, regenerative brakes, anti-theft alarm, IP54
products.summary: TechRadar found the 2.5-inch-thick fat tyres give amazing shock absorption, so the rider doesn't need to weave round small potholes and cracks. It adds regenerative brakes, always-on lights, zero-start for safety and an anti-theft alarm that's uncommon at this price, though it isn't sleek or lightweight (about 44.75lb).
pros: Amazing shock absorption from fat tyres

products.name: Kirin G3
products.best_for: Off-road, private-land use where you want maximum speed and hill power (far faster than UK rental limits)
products.key_spec: 1200W motor, 936Wh battery, 31mph, 43 miles range, 10.5in off-road tyres, 30° climb
products.summary: TechRadar found speed and acceleration top notch, with no range issues in testing and the ability to zoom up and down hills thanks to the powerful motor. The deck kept feet firmly in place at high speed, though motor control isn't very granular and the on-screen buttons are finicky. It weighs about 55lb, so it's far heavier than the other scooters here.

guide.q: Is it legal to ride a private electric scooter in the UK?
guide.a: Only on private land, with the landowner's permission. The Metropolitan Police advises it isn't currently possible to insure a privately owned e-scooter, so it's illegal to use one on the road or in public spaces such as parks, pavements and shopping centres. Rental scooters that are part of an official ride-share scheme can be used on public roads.

guide.q: How long will the battery last in real use?
guide.a: A handful of scooters last a week between charges, but most commuter scooters give two or three days. As TechRadar's example, an 18-mile scooter should last about three days at a three-mile average per trip, but needs charging every night if you ride more than about eight miles per trip. Riding fast also drains the battery quickly, as with the Pure models here.

guide.q: Can I ride an electric scooter in the rain?
guide.a: It depends on the ingress protection (IP) rating. The Pure Air models here are IP65 (dust-tight and protected against water jets) and the NIU is IP54. TechRadar notes that even IPX5 or IPX6 rated commuter scooters aren't recommended for heavy rain or flooding, and only an IPX7 or higher rating survives submersion.

Braking is very important, especially in hilly areas, where a dual braking system is more reliable and safer than a single brake. Also consider tyre type (air-filled tyres give better stability and traction than solid ones), lights and reflectors, and hill grade rating, which is typically 15-20% on commuter scooters.
